journal.title: Journal
journal.intro: Plain answers to what tenants and owners ask us, with the rules checked against GOV.UK and dated.

items.title: What you pay to move in
items.summary: Three payments, and nothing else: what a tenant can be asked for in England, with a worked example.

p: To move into a home let in England you can be asked for three things: a holding deposit, a tenancy deposit and your rent. Referencing, admin, check-in and check-out fees have been banned since the Tenant Fees Act 2019.
A holding deposit reserves the home while checks are done. It can be no more than one week's rent, which is the yearly rent divided by 52.

sections.h: The deposit: five weeks, or six
p: Where the rent is under £50,000 a year, the tenancy deposit can be no more than five weeks' rent. From £50,000 to £100,000 a year, it can be up to six weeks'.
Homes let for more than £100,000 a year aren't covered by these rules; the terms are agreed in writing instead.

sections.h: Rent in advance: one month, after you sign
p: Since 1 May 2026 a landlord or agent can't ask for or accept rent before you've signed the tenancy agreement. Once you have, they can ask for up to one month's rent in advance.

sections.h: The advertised rent is the rent
p: A home must be advertised with its rent, and the landlord can't encourage or accept offers above it. If you're asked to bid, you can say no.
For a rent of £2,500 a month (£30,000 a year), a week's rent is £576.92. The holding deposit can be up to £576; the tenancy deposit up to £2,884 (five weeks); the first month is £2,500.
With your agreement the holding deposit goes towards the first month, so before the keys you'd pay £5,384 in all. Our fees page works this out for any rent.

items.title: Your deposit: protected in 30 days, back in 10
items.summary: Where a deposit goes, what you must be told, and how it comes back at the end.

p: A tenancy deposit must be put in a government-approved scheme within 30 days of the landlord or agent getting it. In England there are three: the Deposit Protection Service, MyDeposits and the Tenancy Deposit Scheme.

Within the same 30 days the tenant must be told: the address of the home; how much they paid; how it's protected; the scheme's name and contact details, and its dispute service; the landlord's or agent's contact details; anyone else who paid part of it; why some of it might be kept; how to ask for it back; what to do if the landlord can't be reached; and what happens if you disagree about the amount.
Our move-in planner puts the 30th day in your calendar, so you know when to ask if it hasn't arrived.

Once you both agree how much comes back, it must be returned within 10 days. If you don't agree, the money stays protected in the scheme until the dispute is settled, and the scheme's free dispute service can decide it.

Under the rules in force since 1 May 2026, a court will generally only grant possession where the deposit was protected in a scheme, or has been returned, or a claim about it has been settled. Protecting it on time protects you too.

sources.title: Information you must give to your tenants
Renters' Rights Act: an overview for landlords

items.title: Letting your home after 1 May 2026
items.summary: Rolling tenancies, no Section 21, rent reviews once a year: what changed for owners, and what it means in practice.

p: From 1 May 2026, assured shorthold tenancies became assured periodic tenancies, and every new tenancy is one. They roll from month to month and have no end date.
Section 21, the "no fault" notice, has gone. To end a tenancy a landlord gives a Section 8 notice on one or more grounds set out in law. The usual notice is four months; some grounds are shorter.

You can't use the grounds for selling the home or moving back in during the first 12 months of a tenancy. A tenant can leave with two months' notice in writing, or sooner if you both agree in writing.

sections.h: Rent reviews: once a year, with Form 4A
p: Rent can go up no more than once a year, and not in a tenancy's first 12 months. The increase is proposed on Form 4A with at least two months' notice, and a tenant can challenge an increase above the open-market rent.
Advertise the rent you want and accept that rent: offers above it can't be invited or accepted. No rent can be taken before the agreement is signed, and no more than a month in advance after.
Tenants can ask to keep a pet; you can refuse only for a good reason.

Our agreements, notices and rent reviews follow these rules, and we tell you before a date matters: a rent review's two months, a renewal of the gas safety record, an inspection. Ask us about any of it.

items.title: A top-floor flat that had sat empty for a winter
items.home: Two-bedroom mansion flat, St John's Wood
items.before: Listed elsewhere at a rent above the block, with photographs taken at dusk. Three months without an offer.
items.did: Re-photographed in daylight, priced from the four lets in the block that year, and shown on Saturdays when the porter is on.
items.after: Let agreed in eleven days. The same tenants have stayed through two rent reviews.

items.title: A Regency floor that kept flooding the flat below
items.home: First-floor flat in a Kensington terrace
items.before: Three leaks in a year from an old overflow, and a neighbour's claim each time.
items.did: Our contractor traced it to the roof gully, fixed it with the freeholder's consent and photographed it before and after; we check it at every inspection.
items.after: No leaks since, and the neighbour's insurer closed the file.

items.title: An owner abroad who wanted one statement
items.home: A house in Marylebone, let floor by floor
items.before: Five tenancies, five dates, and rent arriving in five different weeks.
items.did: Moved every tenancy to the same rent day at renewal, and one statement each month with every floor on it.
items.after: One payment, one statement, on the same day each month.
